prompt: Given an abstract Shape class and a finished Circle subclass, complete ShapeMath: a nested static Rect subclass (width x height) and a static totalArea method that sums the areas of a mixed Shape array. Area checks are rounded to 2 decimals.
explanation: An abstract class fixes a contract (every Shape has an area()) without providing an implementation, so each concrete subclass supplies its own formula. totalArea works on Shape[] and never needs to know which concrete class each element is: calling s.area() dispatches to Circle's or Rect's version at runtime. A nested static class like ShapeMath.Rect is an ordinary class that simply lives inside another class's namespace.
hints: Rect needs two final double fields set in the constructor; area() is just width * height.
In totalArea, loop over the array with for (Shape s : shapes) and accumulate s.area() into a double sum.
You never need instanceof here -- polymorphism picks the right area() for each element.
